# luminous_ui — Project Docs & Continuation System

This `docs/` tree is the **durable memory of the project**. It exists so any new
Claude Code session (or human) can resume work **without reloading the whole
codebase into context**. Read this file first, then load only the docs relevant
to your task.

> **These docs are a guide, not a rulebook.** They capture the current best plan
> and the *reasoning* behind it — not a fixed process to execute blindly. If,
> while working, the code or new context reveals a better or simpler approach,
> **propose it**: say what you'd change and why, and (once it's the direction)
> update the affected doc + record the shift in `decisions.md`. The plans exist
> to be improved, not obeyed. What must be preserved is the *rationale* and the
> *update trail*, so the next session understands why things are the way they are.

## New session? Resume protocol

1. Read **`progress.md`** — the single source of truth for *what's done, what's
   in flight, and where to pick up* (the **Resume point**).
2. Skim **`roadmap.md`** for the big picture (the five phases).
3. Open only the **`workstreams/<area>.md`** you're working on, plus any
   **`reference/`** file it points to. Do **not** read the other workstreams.
4. Follow **`conventions.md`** — especially the sub-agent policy and the
   end-of-session doc-update ritual.

## File map

| File | What it's for |
|---|---|
| `progress.md` | Living status + session log + the current **resume point**. Update every session. |
| `roadmap.md` | The phased plan (P1→P5) and dependencies. |
| `decisions.md` | Decision log (why we chose what) + locked assumptions. |
| `conventions.md` | How we work: sub-agents, doc ritual, code/test/commit rules. |
| `workstreams/backend-data.md` | **P1** — Bun+Hono API, tcgdex→D1 ingest, R2 images, auth, deck API, lobby DO. Contains the tcgdex API reference. |
| `workstreams/deck-builder.md` | **P2** — real cards in the builder, richer filters, editor + decks list. |
| `workstreams/simulator.md` | **P3** — the rules-driven game engine. |
| `workstreams/online.md` | **P4** — run the simulator over the lobby DO for real matches. |
| `workstreams/polish.md` | **P5** — profiles, avatars, lobby names, misc refinement. |
| `reference/ptcg-rules.md` | Condensed Pokémon TCG ruleset — the spec for the simulator (P3). |

## The one rule that keeps this working

**Keep context small.** Delegate research, code-mapping, and multi-file edits to
sub-agents (see `conventions.md`), load only the workstream you need, and write
what you learned back into these docs **before the session ends**.

2	
3	Five phases. Each has a detailed workstream doc; this is the map + dependencies.
4	Live status lives in `progress.md`, not here.
5	
6	## Phase 1 — Backend & Data Foundation → `workstreams/backend-data.md`
7	Stand up the Bun + Hono API on Cloudflare. Ingest real tcgdex card data into D1,
8	mirror images to R2, add accounts + auth (email/password + Discord/Google),
9	persist decks/folders, and stand up the lobby Durable Object (WebSocket) server.
10	**Unblocks everything else.**
11

13	Replace the fixture card pool with the live catalog API. Complete the deck
14	editor (add/remove, counts, format validation, save/load) and the decks list
15	page (folders, CRUD, persistence). Upgrade filters using the richer tcgdex
16	fields (set/serie, rarity, HP, illustrator, regulation mark, ability/attack text,
17	energy cost).
18	*Depends on: P1 catalog + deck API.*
19	
20	## Phase 3 — Simulator Engine → `workstreams/simulator.md`
21	Research the official Pokémon TCG rules (`reference/ptcg-rules.md`) and build the
22	game engine: a deterministic state machine + a card-effect system driven by the
23	imported card data + descriptions. Iterative — accuracy improves pass over pass;
24	unimplemented cards degrade gracefully. The goal is to replicate the real game.
25	*Depends on: P2 (real, usable decks) + the ruleset.*
26	
27	## Phase 4 — Online Matches → `workstreams/online.md`
28	Run the P3 engine authoritatively inside the lobby Durable Object so two players
29	on different machines can play a real game. Swap the client lobby transport from
30	BroadcastChannel to WebSocket. Same engine as local play, with tweaks for
31	authority/hidden info.
32	*Depends on: P3 engine + P1 lobby DO.*
33	
34	## Phase 5 — Polish → `workstreams/polish.md`
35	Now that user + card data exist: player names & profile pictures on the lobby,
36	profiles, real deck-cover art, and general refinement. Threads through P2–P4 but
37	tracked separately so it isn't forgotten.

# Roadmap

Five phases. Each has a detailed workstream doc; this is the map + dependencies.
Live status lives in `progress.md`, not here.

## Phase 1 — Backend & Data Foundation → `workstreams/backend-data.md`
Stand up the Bun + Hono API on Cloudflare. Ingest real tcgdex card data into D1,
mirror images to R2, add accounts + auth (email/password + Discord/Google),
persist decks/folders, and stand up the lobby Durable Object (WebSocket) server.
**Unblocks everything else.**

## Phase 2 — Deck Builder & Decks List (real cards) → `workstreams/deck-builder.md`
Replace the fixture card pool with the live catalog API. Complete the deck
editor (add/remove, counts, format validation, save/load) and the decks list
page (folders, CRUD, persistence). Upgrade filters using the richer tcgdex
fields (set/serie, rarity, HP, illustrator, regulation mark, ability/attack text,
energy cost).
*Depends on: P1 catalog + deck API.*

## Phase 3 — Simulator Engine → `workstreams/simulator.md`
Research the official Pokémon TCG rules (`reference/ptcg-rules.md`) and build the
game engine: a deterministic state machine + a card-effect system driven by the
imported card data + descriptions. Iterative — accuracy improves pass over pass;
unimplemented cards degrade gracefully. The goal is to replicate the real game.
*Depends on: P2 (real, usable decks) + the ruleset.*

## Phase 4 — Online Matches → `workstreams/online.md`
Run the P3 engine authoritatively inside the lobby Durable Object so two players
on different machines can play a real game. Swap the client lobby transport from
BroadcastChannel to WebSocket. Same engine as local play, with tweaks for
authority/hidden info.
*Depends on: P3 engine + P1 lobby DO.*

## Phase 5 — Polish → `workstreams/polish.md`
Now that user + card data exist: player names & profile pictures on the lobby,
profiles, real deck-cover art, and general refinement. Threads through P2–P4 but
tracked separately so it isn't forgotten.
*Depends on: P1 user data.*

1	# Working Conventions
2	
3	## Guidance, not gospel
4	These docs are a **living guide**, not a fixed process. You have context the
5	planning sessions didn't — the actual code, real data, what just broke. Use it:
6	- **Suggest better/different approaches** when you see them. Don't follow a task
7	  list off a cliff because it's written down.
8	- When you deviate: **explain the what + why**, prefer aligning with the user on
9	  anything significant, then **update the affected doc** and log the change in
10	  `decisions.md` (with its rationale). Small in-the-flow improvements don't need
11	  ceremony — just keep the docs honest.
12	- Locked assumptions and D-numbered decisions are **defaults with reasons**, not
13	  laws. Revisit any of them freely; the only hard rule is *don't reverse one
14	  silently* — leave a trail.
15	- Treat file/symbol references in these docs as **point-in-time** — verify against
16	  the current code before relying on them.
17	
18	## Context hygiene (the point of this whole system)
19	- Load **`progress.md` + the one relevant `workstreams/*.md`** (+ its
20	  `reference/`). Don't read unrelated workstreams or sweep the repo.
21	- Prefer facts already written in these docs over re-deriving them.
22	
23	## Sub-agent / workflow policy
24	Delegate to sub-agents to keep the main session's context lean:
25	- **Research** (rules, library docs, API behaviour) → a `general-purpose` agent
26	  that writes a condensed doc into `reference/` and returns only a summary.

# Working Conventions

## Guidance, not gospel
These docs are a **living guide**, not a fixed process. You have context the
planning sessions didn't — the actual code, real data, what just broke. Use it:
- **Suggest better/different approaches** when you see them. Don't follow a task
  list off a cliff because it's written down.
- When you deviate: **explain the what + why**, prefer aligning with the user on
  anything significant, then **update the affected doc** and log the change in
  `decisions.md` (with its rationale). Small in-the-flow improvements don't need
  ceremony — just keep the docs honest.
- Locked assumptions and D-numbered decisions are **defaults with reasons**, not
  laws. Revisit any of them freely; the only hard rule is *don't reverse one
  silently* — leave a trail.
- Treat file/symbol references in these docs as **point-in-time** — verify against
  the current code before relying on them.

## Context hygiene (the point of this whole system)
- Load **`progress.md` + the one relevant `workstreams/*.md`** (+ its
  `reference/`). Don't read unrelated workstreams or sweep the repo.
- Prefer facts already written in these docs over re-deriving them.

## Sub-agent / workflow policy
Delegate to sub-agents to keep the main session's context lean:
- **Research** (rules, library docs, API behaviour) → a `general-purpose` agent
  that writes a condensed doc into `reference/` and returns only a summary.
- **Code mapping** ("how does X work today, what's missing") → an **Explore**
  agent (read-only; returns conclusions, not file dumps).
- **Implementation** of a self-contained slice → a `general-purpose` agent with
  a tight spec; it edits files and returns a summary + what to verify.
- **Review** before committing non-trivial work → `/code-review`.
- **Big fan-out** (e.g. authoring effect handlers for many cards, or a broad
  audit) → a **Workflow** (multi-agent). Note: user-triggered/opt-in — ask first.

Rule of thumb: if answering would mean reading many files, delegate it and keep
only the conclusion.

## Code & quality
- TypeScript strict; match the surrounding code's style and comment density.
- **Biome** for lint/format; **Vitest** for tests. Run **`bun run check`**
  (tsc + biome lint + vitest) before calling work done.
- Pure logic gets unit tests (see the many `*.test.ts` in the repo); DOM tests
  opt into jsdom per-file (`// @vitest-environment jsdom`).

## Git / commits
- Branch off `main` for non-trivial work; commit/push only when asked.
- Commit trailer per global config: `Co-Authored-By: Claude ...`.

## End-of-session ritual (do not skip)
1. Update `progress.md`: status table + session-log entry + **new resume point**.
2. Record any decision in `decisions.md`.
3. Write anything learned into the right workstream/reference doc so the next
   session doesn't rediscover it.

Lands **Ortega** ×2 (sv03-190/-219, the Miriam shape with both halves across the table) and **Greavard** "Underworld Stroll" (sv01-105) DERIVED from attack text — its Supporter-filtered twin has no second sentence, and its plain second attack (Sharp Fang) is exactly why the per-CARD registry `attack` field could not have carried it. `programPlayable` gained the empty-opponent-hand gate (a PUBLIC count — the Catcher/Hammer class, not Poké Ball's; it reads hand LENGTH and never the filter, since whether a hidden hand holds a match is what the game state does not establish) and is now EXPORTED, so the HUD greys a dead Trainer/Ability row with the predicate that rejects it. |
72	
73	**Long tail (~70 single-card ops)** — e.g. `bounceToHand` (Penny), `moveDamageCounters`
74	(Slowbro), `healBothPlayers` (Picnic Basket), `noRetreatCostAura` (Clefable ex),
75	`removeWeakness` (Florges), `retaliationDamage` (Rocky Helmet), `preventDamageFromExV`
76	(Mimikyu), the Iono/Judge prize-count draws, per-card search filters
77	(`searchFilter:{itemCard,toolCard,evolutionPokemon,…}`), and several bespoke
78	passives/triggers. Full list in the fan-out result. Many collapse into a few
79	parameterized ops (an `attachEnergyFrom` with source/filter params; a
80	`conditionalGate` family; extra `CardFilter` kinds), so the real op count to build
81	is well under 70.
82	
83	## Suggested sequencing
84	1. ✅ **`attachEnergyFrom`** — the single biggest unlock (11+, and the engine of most
85	   evolving-deck Abilities). **DONE 4/11** (engine 0.14.0: single-attach + the
86	   targetType/bonusCounters/notIfKO/basicOnly/multi/endsTurn riders — Quaquaval,
87	   Baxcalibur, Gardevoir ex, Koraidon ex). The rest need a deck-search source /
88	   `lookAtTopN` / per-card riders.
89	2. ✅ **`discardPileRetrieval`** — **DONE 3/6** (engine 0.15.0, the searchDeck mirror
90	   + `supporter`/`pokemonOrBasicEnergy` filters: Energy Retrieval, Pal Pad, Super
91	   Rod). Extra `CardFilter` kinds (Item/Tool/Evolution/no-rule-box) still layer on
92	   for other searchers.
93	3. ✅ **`lookAtTopN`** — **DONE 2/5** (engine 0.16.0: Great Ball, Pokégear 3.0 —
94	   the reveal-to-hand core). A from-the-top **attach** variant then unblocks
95	   Electric Generator / Hydreigon (also 2 of the remaining attachEnergyFrom cards).
96	4. ✅ **`moveEnergy`** — **DONE 2/5** (engine 0.17.0: Energy Switch, Poppy — the
97	   own→own core, the interpreter's first compound-park op + the `anyEnergy` filter).
98	   The remaining 3 layer riders on it: a fixed-endpoint provided-type move
99	   (Armarouge), an opponent-side move on evolve (Mismagius), an on-KO Tool move
100	   (Exp. Share). Next candidates: the from-the-top **attach** variant (Electric
101	   Generator / Hydreigon, also 2 attachEnergyFrom cards), the **`conditionalPlay`**
102	   family (5), or the **hand-refresh Supporter family** (Iono/Judge/Marnie).
103	5. ✅ The **hand-refresh Supporter family** — **DONE, row CLOSED** (engine 0.18.0, the
104	   `handRefresh` op: the whole `shuffleHandIntoDeck` row — Youngster / Brassius /
105	   Katy — **plus Judge**, the first op to affect the OPPONENT's hand/deck; and it
106	   closes the `endTurn` row via the Trainer-path `trainerEndsTurn` fold; then engine
107	   0.19.0 added **Iono** as three riders — `toBottom` (deck order survives),
108	   `prizeCount` draw, `onlyIfAnyMoved` gate). No Marnie in the sv01–03 catalog.
109	6. ✅ **`conditionalPlay` / `conditionalGate`** — **PRIMITIVE DONE** (engine
110	   0.20.0): one `BoardCondition` vocabulary with two consumers — the
111	   `trainerPlayableIf` PLAY gate and the `conditionGate` branch op — plus
112	   `drawUntilHandSize`. Lands **Fighting Au Lait**, **Falkner** and **Grusha**.
113	   Every remaining gated card needs a second missing piece (see the row above),
114	   so the primitive is done but the row is not. Cheapest next readers of the same
115	   vocabulary: ~~**Defiance Band**~~ (**DONE**, engine 0.42.0 — the conditional PASSIVE, the third consumer) and
116	   ~~**Dendra**~~ (**DONE**, engine 0.27.0 — the choose-from-hand → bottom-of-deck park, which turned out to be the §7.5 hand cost with a second destination rather than a new op).
117	7. ✅ **`discardOpponentEnergy`** — **DONE 3/4** (engine 0.21.0, the `discardEnergy`
118	   op + the `specialEnergy` filter: Crushing Hammer, Giacomo, Mawile). Building it
119	   surfaced the next big structural unlock, now its own row above: **attack effect
120	   programs cannot PARK**, which alone blocks ~13 more cards in the SAME family
121	   (every "Discard an Energy from this Pokémon" attack, plus the opponent-side
122	   attack twins of Crushing Hammer). Klawf ex, the 4th card on this row, needs
123	   `onDamagedByAttack` instead.
124	8. ✅ **attack effect programs that can PARK** — **DONE** (engine 0.22.0, the
125	   `attackEpilogue` stage + `discardEnergy`'s `yourActive` / `count:"all"` arms:
126	   12 catalog rows, all DERIVED from the printed sentence, no registry rows). The
127	   structural half is what matters — every future attack effect may now hold a
128	   decision. The remaining self-discard prints need op vocabulary, not park work:
129	   an **exact-N** discard (Corviknight 2, Koraidon 3) and an **energy-of-type**
130	   filter (Kilowattrel's "a {L} Energy", where {L} means *provides* {L}).
131	9. ✅ **The discardEnergy ATTACK arms** — **DONE** (engine 0.23.0): the
132	   opponent-side twins (bare + coin-gated) and the exact-N `count`, **11 catalog
133	   rows for two deriver sentences and one widened field, zero registry rows.**
134	   What is left of the whole energy-discard family is now ONE missing primitive,
135	   a **`providesEnergy` CardFilter** ("an Energy that PROVIDES {X}" — NOT
136	   `basicEnergy` + type, since a Special Energy providing {L} counts and a
137	   {C}-providing one does not). It closes **Kilowattrel, Arcanine ex ×2,
138	   Charmeleon, Charizard** here and also unblocks **Armarouge**'s benched→Active
139	   {R} move (a `moveEnergy` rider) — the same filter read by two ops, the D40
140	   two-consumers shape. The remaining prints after that need sentence STRUCTURE,
141	   not filters: Sandaconda/Eiscue ex/Weavile (a rider clause after the discard)
142	   and Krookodile (a flip-until-tails repeat count).
143	10. ✅ **The `providesEnergy` filter** — **DONE** (engine 0.24.0): "an Energy that
144	   PROVIDES {X}", read by TWO ops — the DERIVED typed self-discard (5 catalog rows,
145	   zero registry rows) and `moveEnergy`'s new `benchToActive` route (Armarouge, 2
146	   rows). It is the first filter a card alone cannot answer: provision is a
147	   while-attached property, and a wildcard Special (Luminous) is an Energy of every
148	   type until another Special demotes it to {C}. Single-sourced with the §8.2 cost
149	   matcher, so what can PAY a {L} cost is exactly what a "{L} Energy" effect can
150	   take. **The whole energy-removal family is now filter-complete**: every card
151	   still unauthored in it is blocked by sentence STRUCTURE (an optional discard
152	   buying an effect, a variable count with damage scaling, a rider clause, a repeat
153	   count) rather than by any missing predicate.
154	11. ✅ **`attachFromTop`** (engine 0.25.0 — Electric Generator / Hydreigon) and
155	   ✅ **`discardFromHandCost`** (engine 0.26.0 — Ultra Ball / Earthen Vessel /
156	   Revavroom / Tinkaton, + Meowscarada ex and Radiant Blastoise migrated off the
157	   removed `AbilityProgram.cost` field: 9 catalog rows). The second shares the
158	   printed wording "You can use this card only if…" but is NOT a `BoardCondition`
159	   — it is a COST with a card CHOICE, so it PARKS, and it is the first op of its
160	   program because the payment is observable before what it buys.
161	12. ✅ **The FLOOR, and the payment that is not a discard** — **DONE** (engine
162	   0.27.0). Two mandatory-exactly-N fixes, one on each prompt that could still say
163	   "up to": `choosePokemonMulti` gained `min`/`max` + `declinable` (rules doc

166	   `discardFromHandCost` became **`payFromHand`** with a required `to`, landing

168	13. ✅ **op→op data flow** — **DONE** (engine 0.28.0), and it closed BOTH deferrals
169	   this family had left, with **5 catalog rows for one mechanism**: **Superior
170	   Energy Retrieval** ×2 ("you can't choose a card you discarded with the effect
171	   of this card" → `discardPileRetrieval.exclude`) and **Miriam** ×3 ("if you
172	   shuffled any cards into your deck in this way, draw 3" → the new `recordGate`),
173	   plus **Dendra**'s printed "if you do", which the vocabulary could not state
174	   before. An op files the uids it MOVED under a named `EffectSlot`; a later op
175	   reads them. The record rides `EffectContinuation` rather than `EffectContext`
176	   (an accumulator, sibling to `rest` — the context is a constant), and it is
177	   keyed by SLOT rather than by position because Miriam prints a deck shuffle
178	   BETWEEN the retrieval and the clause referring to it. Rules doc **§9.2**.
179	14. **Next candidates** *(as written at D48; all three named here have since
180	   landed — Janine's Secret Art in 0.29.0, Saguaro in 0.31.0, Ortega in 0.32.0.
181	   Kept for the reasoning, not the pointer.)*: **Janine's Secret Art**
182	   (sv06.5-059/-088) is the single best-supported row on the board — it needs a
183	   per-target deck search, the first printed "choose **up to** N Pokémon" (the
184	   other end of the range §9.1 added), AND an "in this way" gate (§9.2, which now
185	   exists), so two of its three pieces are built. Otherwise: ~~**Defiance Band**~~
186	   (**DONE**, engine 0.42.0 — the conditional PASSIVE, the D40 vocabulary's third
187	   consumer), or **Saguaro** (the
188	   cheapest reader of "choose up to N Pokémon" alone — `healChosen` widened with a

190	Each is a normal engine slice (new op + interpreter case + registry rows +
191	tests + review), and each turns dozens of "needs-op" rows into a few data rows.

# Simulator coverage — the new-op backlog (P3-M5)

The engine simulates cards as **data-driven op programs** (registry.ts). A card
is playable when its printed effect maps onto the op vocabulary
(`effects.ts` EffectOp, plus the continuous/energy/ability shapes in
`registry.ts`). M4 built the vocabulary through nine slices; M5 expands **card
coverage** across the SV-era pool.

## Method — a classify → verify Workflow fan-out (2026-07-19)
The 140 un-authored **sv01–sv03** Trainers (61), Special Energies (4) and
Pokémon Abilities (75) were classified by a 10-agent fan-out (5 batches ×
classify + adversarial verify), each card judged against the current op
vocabulary with the deriver doctrine — **exact map or flag** (a wrong-but-plausible
program is worse than a flag). Every authorable program was then hand-verified
against the local catalog before landing.

## Result
| Verdict | Count |
|---|---|
| **authorable now** (landed this pass) | **5** |
| needs a new op (backlog below) | 113 |
| already authored (M4) | 22 |
| **total classified** | 140 |

Only ~4% of the un-authored pool is expressible with today's ops — coverage is
**op-bound, not authoring-bound**: each new primitive unlocks a whole family, so
the backlog below (ranked by cards-unlocked) is the roadmap for the next slices.
Authoring is then a few registry rows per card, exactly as D8 intended.

### Authored this pass (M5 #1)
| Card | id | Program |
|---|---|---|
| Poké Ball | sv01-185 | Item — `coinFlipGate → [searchDeck anyPokemon→hand, shuffleDeck]` |
| Pokémon Catcher | sv01-187 | Item — `coinFlipGate → [gust]` |
| Nemona | sv01-180 | Supporter — `drawCards 3` |
| Copperajah ex (Bronze Body) | sv02-150 | passive `damageReductionAfterWR: 30` |
| Stonjourner (Exoskeleton) | sv01-121 | passive `damageReductionAfterWR: 20` |

(The fan-out mis-placed Poké Ball's `shuffleDeck` *after* the coin gate — it must
be *inside* it, or a tails play reorders the deck; fixed + pinned by a test.)

## New-op backlog — ranked by cards unlocked (sv01–03)
Build these to expand coverage; the count is how many classified cards each
unblocks. High-value ops first.

| New op / capability | Cards | Example cards |
|---|---:|---|
| 🚧 **`attachEnergyFrom`** (attach Energy from hand/discard/deck to a chosen Pokémon) | 11 | **DONE 4/11: Quaquaval, Baxcalibur** (single attach from hand/discard, engine 0.12.0) + **Gardevoir ex** (the `targetType`/`bonusCounters`/`notIfKO` riders, engine 0.13.0) + **Koraidon ex "Dino Cry"** (multi-attach = N ops + `basicOnly` + the `endsTurn` fold, engine 0.14.0). Remaining 7 need MORE ops on top: Forretress ex (deck-search + self-KO), Charizard ex (onEvolve + deck-search-multi), Geeta (deck-search + can't-attack), Electric Generator/Hydreigon (need `lookAtTopN`), Pawmot (deck-search→self, needs the source uid in EffectContext), Wigglytuff (a Special Energy by name) |
| ✅ **`discardPileRetrieval`** (put/shuffle cards from discard → hand/deck) | 6 | **DONE 5/6** — engine 0.15.0 landed the core (the searchDeck mirror + `supporter`/`pokemonOrBasicEnergy` filters): **Energy Retrieval** (2 Basic Energy → hand), **Pal Pad** (2 Supporters → deck), **Super Rod** (3 Pokémon/Basic Energy → deck); engine 0.28.0's §9.2 op→op record landed the two that had to read their own earlier clause: **Superior Energy Retrieval** ×2 (the new `exclude` rider — the cost pays INTO this pile, so without it the payment refunds itself) and **Miriam** ×3 (the new `recordAs` rider + a `recordGate` two ops downstream). Remaining 1: **Pelipper** (an Ability, not a Trainer). |
| ✅ **`lookAtTopN`** (reveal/take a matching card from the top N) | 5 | **DONE 2/5** (engine 0.16.0, the top-of-deck twin of searchDeck: candidates are the top-N matches, then a trailing shuffle): **Great Ball** (top 7 → a Pokémon), **Pokégear 3.0** (top 7 → a Supporter). Remaining 3 need MORE: Electric Generator + Hydreigon attach the found Energy (a from-the-top **attach** variant — the 2 attachEnergyFrom cards this also unblocks), Malamar peeks at the OPPONENT's deck top (a distinct info-only op). |
| ✅ **`moveEnergy`** (move an Energy between your Pokémon) | 5 | **DONE 3/5** (engine 0.17.0, the compound-park own→own op + the `anyEnergy` filter): **Energy Switch** (a Basic Energy, max 1), **Poppy** (up to 2 any Energy, max 2), and — engine 0.24.0, the `route: "benchToActive"` rider + the `providesEnergy` filter — **Armarouge** "Fire Off" (a {R} Energy benched→Active, as often as you like). Remaining 2 need MORE: Mismagius "Magical Flick" (moves the OPPONENT's Energy on evolve — opponent-side + onEvolve trigger), Exp. Share (an on-KO Tool trigger). |
| ✅ **`conditionalPlay`** (a "you can use this only if <board condition>" gate) | 5 | **PRIMITIVE DONE, 1/5 cards** (engine 0.20.0 — the `BoardCondition` vocabulary + its two consumers: the `trainerPlayableIf` PLAY gate and the `conditionGate` branch op): **Fighting Au Lait** (more Prizes left → heal 60). The same vocabulary also lands **Falkner** (Stadium → draw 2 more) and, with `drawUntilHandSize`, **Grusha** — 2 cards from other rows. Remaining 4 each need a SECOND missing piece: **Letter of Encouragement** (a "were any of your Pokémon KO'd during your opponent's LAST turn" state fact — new per-seat history + flow wiring), ~~**Dendra**~~ (**DONE**, engine 0.27.0 — the gate turned out to be §7.5's hand COST, not a `BoardCondition`: `payFromHand` `to: "deckBottom"` + `drawUntilHandSize`), **Luxray** (an in-hand Ability surface — abilities are in-play only today), **Lunatone** (Stadium-effect prevention). Next reader of the same vocabulary: ~~**Defiance Band**~~ (**DONE**, engine 0.42.0 — the conditional PASSIVE, the third consumer, reusing `morePrizesThanOpponent`). |
| ✅ **`discardOpponentEnergy`** (discard an Energy from an opponent's Pokémon) | 4 | **DONE 3/4** (engine 0.21.0 — the `discardEnergy` op + the `specialEnergy` filter; ONE op whose `from` names both the eligible Pokémon and how many are hit, all three arms landing with a real card): **Crushing Hammer** (`opponentChosen`, behind a coin flip), **Giacomo** (`opponentEach` — one Special Energy off EVERY one of their Pokémon that has one), **Mawile** (`opponentActive`, an onPlayToBench trigger). Remaining 1: **Klawf ex**, which needs `onDamagedByAttack` (the row below), not more of this op. |
| ✅ **attack effect programs that can PARK** (a mid-attack `effect:choose`) | ~13 | **DONE — the mechanism (engine 0.22.0), plus 12 catalog rows of its first family.** A new `attackEpilogue` PendingStage carries the §8.1 KO sweep + the §5.3 turn end; `attack.ts` seeds it BEFORE the effect program runs and folds through `settleProgram`'s `resumeTail`, so a parked prompt and the ops behind it survive. Landed with it: `discardEnergy` gained a **`yourActive`** arm and a **`count: "all"`** rider, both DERIVED from the printed sentence (no registry rows) — "Discard an Energy from this Pokémon." covers **Houndoom ×2 (sv01-034, sv03-133), Charcadet, Staraptor, Paldean Tauros, Dedenne ex ×2, Bombirdier**; "Discard all Energy from this Pokémon." covers **Pawmot ×2, Raichu ×2**. |
| ✅ **the discardEnergy ATTACK arms** — the opponent-side twins + the exact-N count | 11 | **DONE (engine 0.23.0), again with ZERO registry rows — two deriver sentences and one widened field.** The **twins** ("Discard an Energy from your opponent's Active Pokémon.", bare and behind a flip) run the EXISTING `opponentActive` arm with an `anyEnergy` filter: **Pincurchin** (sv02-072), **Gumshoos** (sv03-177), **Dragonite V ×2** (swsh10.5-049/-076); **Dedenne** (sv01-094), **Maschiff** (sv01-136), **Tympole** (sv03-050), **Yveltal** (sv06.5-035). The **exact-N** self-discard widens `count` from `"all"` to any number: **Corviknight** (sv02-148), **Slither Wing** (sv06.5-026), **Koraidon** (sv01-124). The prompt's `scope` became `{kind:"total",count} \| {kind:"each"}` and the interchangeable collapse now keeps `count` reps per class. STILL BLOCKED after it: the **TYPED** discards (closed by the row below), the multi-sentence riders (**Sandaconda**, **Eiscue ex**, **Weavile**), and **Krookodile**'s flip-until-tails repeat count. |
| ✅ **the `providesEnergy` CardFilter** — "an Energy that PROVIDES {X}" | 7 | **DONE (engine 0.24.0) — the last missing piece of the energy-discard family, and the first filter a CARD alone cannot answer.** "{L} Energy" is not "a Basic Lightning card": a Special providing {L} IS one, a wildcard (Luminous) is one of EVERY type, and provision is a while-ATTACHED property that Luminous's own text makes depend on the holder's other attachments — so the predicate reads what an Energy gives ON ITS HOST, through the very code §8.2's cost matcher reads (`unitsProvidedBy`). `matchesFilter`, the deck/hand/discard scanner, answers FALSE for it (a card in a pile is attached to nothing), so authoring it into a pile-scanning op is a loud no-op rather than a wrong card. TWO consumers, one vocabulary (the D40 shape): the **typed self-discard**, DERIVED in both printed notations — the modern "{R}" and the swsh-era spelled-out "Fire" — for **Kilowattrel** (sv01-079), **Arcanine ex ×2** (sv01-032/-224), **Charmeleon** (swsh10.5-009) and **Charizard** (swsh10.5-010) with ZERO registry rows; and **`moveEnergy`'s `benchToActive` route**, authoring **Armarouge ×2** (sv01-041/-203). STILL BLOCKED, and now every one of them for sentence STRUCTURE rather than for any missing filter: **Pawmot ex** (a typed discard plus "220 damage to 1 of your opponent's Pokémon" — `damageChosen` exists but targets the Bench, not any Pokémon), **Bellibolt ex** ("you may … to make it Paralyzed" — an optional discard BUYING an effect), **Chien-Pao ex** / **Mewtwo VSTAR** (a variable count with damage scaling off it), **Sandaconda** / **Eiscue ex** / **Weavile** (rider clauses) and **Krookodile** (a repeat count). |
| ✅ **`discardFromHandCost`** → **`payFromHand`** (pay N cards out of hand to play) | 4 | **DONE 3/4, and the row's real size was bigger than this count** (engine 0.26.0 — the printed COST that PARKS, so it is an OP at the head of its program rather than a field paid before it). Two printed wordings, ONE mechanism, and the wording tracks where the paying card sits: TRAINERS say "only if you discard 2 **other** cards" because the card is in the hand it pays from — **Ultra Ball** (sv01-196), **Earthen Vessel** (sv06.5-096, "another card"); ABILITIES never say "other" because the card is on the board — **Revavroom** (sv01-142, "an Energy card" → draw to 6, the ORDER witness), **Tinkaton** (sv02-105, "a card" → draw 3, the unfiltered general case). The same sentence is printed on **Meowscarada ex** and **Radiant Blastoise** (swsh10.5-018), so the old `AbilityProgram.cost` field — which could only express the FUNGIBLE case — was REMOVED and Meowscarada migrated onto the op: 9 catalog rows in all. `chooseCards` gained a required `min` (the first MANDATORY card park; every "up to" consumer declares 0). **Row CLOSED at engine 0.28.0**: **Superior Energy Retrieval** (sv02-189/-277) landed with the §9.2 record, its "(You can't choose a card you discarded with the effect of this card.)" becoming `discardPileRetrieval.exclude` reading the uids `payFromHand` filed. |
| **`onDamagedByAttack`** (a trigger firing when damaged by an attack, even if KO'd) | 4 | Cacnea, Cacturne, Armarouge, Klawf ex |
| ✅ **`shuffleHandIntoDeck` (+ draw)** — the Iono/Judge hand-refresh family | 3 | **DONE — row CLOSED, +Judge +Iono** (the `handRefresh` op: engine 0.18.0 fully-automatic, reaches the OPPONENT): **Youngster** (draw 5), **Brassius** (draw hand+1), **Katy** (draw 8 + turn ends), **Judge** (both shuffle + draw 4), and **Iono** (engine 0.19.0 — the `toBottom` placement so the deck's ORDER survives, a `prizeCount` draw, and the `onlyIfAnyMoved` cross-seat draw gate). No Marnie exists in the sv01–03 catalog. The other bottom-of-deck cards: **Dendra** (**DONE** engine 0.27.0 — a CHOSEN card, so it is `payFromHand` `to: "deckBottom"`, not this op) and **Skwovet** ×2 "Nest Stash" (**DONE** engine 0.27.0 — this op exactly, `toBottom` + `onlyIfAnyMoved` + a fixed draw of 1, on the ABILITY path; zero new code). Still open: none — **Ortega** landed in engine 0.32.0 (`bottomFromOpponentHand`, the row below). |
| **`stadiumActivatedAbility`** (a "once during each player's turn" Stadium) | 3 | Artazon, Mesagoza, Town Store |
| **`damageAttacker`** (put counters on the attacking Pokémon) | 3 | Cacnea, Cacturne, Stunfisk |
| **`disableAbilities`** (a continuous Ability-lock aura) | 3 | Klefki, Spiritomb, Ting-Lu ex |
| ✅ `drawUntilHandSize` | 2 | **DONE — row CLOSED 2/2.** (engine 0.20.0 — draws to a floor, never TRIMS a bigger hand; no event at a count ≤ 0): **Grusha** (to 5, or to 7 with no Energy on your board — the `conditionGate` `otherwise` arm), and — engine 0.27.0 — **Dendra** (draw to 5, counting the card just paid to the bottom of the deck: the payment is the program's FIRST op, so a hand of 4 draws three). |
| ✅ `endTurn` (a play that ends your turn) | 2 | **DONE**: Koraidon ex (the `AbilityProgram.endsTurn` fold, engine 0.14.0) + Katy (the same fold on the Trainer path via `trainerEndsTurn`, engine 0.18.0). |
| ✅ `conditionalDamageBonus` (Tool: +N under a condition) | 2 | **DONE — row CLOSED 2/2.** **Defiance Band** (sv01-169, engine 0.42.0): the D40 `BoardCondition` vocabulary's **third consumer and first PASSIVE one** — the conditional twin of Vitality Band. New `PassiveEffects.damageBonusBeforeWRIf {amount, cond}` reusing the EXISTING `morePrizesThanOpponent` (no new condition), so it is a card row + one field, not a new primitive. continuous.ts stays the seat-FREE aggregation point (collects the gated bonuses raw); the fold lives in interpreter.ts `attackerPreWRBonus`, shared by the two pre-W/R read sites (attack.ts main hit + snipeActive) so `conditionHolds` is evaluated once, at the only sites that know the attacker's seat. **Choice Belt** (sv02-176, engine 0.43.0): the TARGET-gated twin — +30 before W/R, but only when the DEFENDER is a Pokémon **V**. 248	      Bouffer reduces). PARKS on a multi-Pokémon choice (choosePokemonMulti) when

250	      the Bench holds `count` or fewer (forced — "choose 2" with 2 available is
251	      both), and is a no-op with an empty opponent Bench. Only raises damage; the
252	      Knock Out check runs in the CALLER'S sweep (flow.ts settleProgram →
253	      resolveMidTurnKnockOuts), a MID-TURN KO that resumes the actor's turn — so
254	      this, like every op, never KOs or touches the flow tail.
255	
256	      **`count` IS EXACT — the printed number is a floor as well as a ceiling.**
257	      "Put 3 damage counters on 1 of your opponent's Benched Pokémon" means one,
258	      not "up to one": a card prints the words "up to" when a partial answer is
259	      legal, and none of this op's consumers does. So the park asks for `count` on
260	      the nose, and the interpreter's forced branch (a Bench no bigger than
261	      `count`) is the same rule under §8.6 "do as much as you can". The floor is
262	      what stops Meowscarada ex from paying its irreversible hand cost and then
263	      placing nothing.
264

266	      TRIGGERED Ability, where the engine auto-fires the trigger (triggers.ts) and
267	      the decline therefore has nowhere else to live but the pick. Hawlucha is the
268	      one consumer: "you may choose 2 …" is all-or-nothing, so the prompt's legal

../../docs/decisions.md:83:| D56 | The "×"/multiply damage family — Pecharunt ex / Annihilape (P3-M5, engine 0.36.0) | The sibling of D54–D55's additive "+" family. **"This attack does N damage for each Prize card your opponent has taken."** (NO "more") is now SIMULATED. Unlike the additive fold, the printed "N×" is the **PER-unit**, so `per × count` is the **WHOLE damage with the printed base DROPPED** (count 0 → 0 damage) — a **DISTINCT fold, not a `count` member**, exactly as D55 predicted. A new reader **`deriveAttackDamageMultiplier`** (effects.ts) + regex **`OPPONENT_PRIZES_MULTIPLY`** (`^This attack does (\d+) damage for each Prize card your opponent has taken\.$`, no "more") parse into the SAME `{per, count: {kind: "opponentPrizesTaken"}}` shape and **reuse D55's count evaluator UNCHANGED** — the two families differ ONLY in attack.ts's fold. attack.ts reads BOTH scaling derivers (`damageMultiplier` only when `damageBonus === null` — the regexes are mutually exclusive on "more", so at most one fires) and **`scaledBase = damageMultiplier !== null ? 0 : base`** drops the base for a multiply while the additive family keeps it; the §8.5 pipeline guard (`scaledBase + scaled > 0`) and `DAMAGE_DEALT.base` both use `scaledBase`. Lands **Pecharunt ex** sv06.5-039 "Irritated Outburst" (60×, {D}{D}) and **Annihilape** sv01-109 "Rage Fist" (70×, {F}) — two pers on one count source. **The bigger "×" siblings stay LOUD, the multiply reader's anchor-guard witnesses:** **Wo-Chien ex** sv02-027 "Covetous Ivy" (a benched-TARGET multiply — "…to 1 of your opponent's Benched Pokémon for each Prize…", refused by the mid-sentence text the anchors exclude) and **Chien-Pao ex** "Hail Blade" (a DISCARDED-Energy count — "…for each card you discarded in this way.", refused by the tail). New `MULTIPLY_DAMAGE_DECK` (Darkness/Fighting Energy pay {D}{D}/{F}; Fire cannot). **No web change** — `DAMAGE_DEALT.base:0, scaled:N` renders through the generic `· scaled +N` breadcrumb. engineVersion 0.35.0 → **0.36.0**; 1653 → **1661** tests, `bun run check` green. **Review (1 read-only adversarial reviewer): NO HIGH, NO MED, no surviving mutants.** Catalog narrowness proven EXHAUSTIVELY (of the 4 cards printing "for each Prize card your opponent has taken", the multiply regex matches ONLY Pecharunt/Annihilape; refuses Wo-Chien benched and Charizard's additive "more"); the base-drop is pinned two ways (a count-0 "no DAMAGE_DEALT" test — a kept base would deal 60 — and a count-2 `{base:0, scaled:120, dealt:120}` test — a kept base would give 180); the captured per is pinned by Annihilape's 70 ≠ Pecharunt's 60. **ONE LOW FOUND AND FIXED:** the Pecharunt fixture's "Verbatim vs the local D1 catalog" comment omitted the card's real "Subjugating Chains" Ability — corrected to an honest "printed STATS + attack row verbatim; Ability OMITTED (unexercised, no registry row)", the false-verbatim defect this repo names explicitly (the Charizard fixture comment). **Recorded, NOT fixed:** the multiply W/R ordering is not INDEPENDENTLY pinned by a weak-defender test (every multiply test uses fix-bigbody, no weakness) — but the fold is the SAME shared pipeline line as the additive family, already pinned by the "folds BEFORE weakness" test, and with `scaledBase` forced to 0 the multiply arm only supplies `scaled`, so it cannot break the order alone (reviewer LOW — the same call D55 made for its Prize arm). *Why: resume item #1, the cheapest continuation — it confirms the "distinct fold" shape D55 deliberately deferred, reuses the count evaluator with zero change, and lands two real headline cards while PRESERVING the anchor-guard discipline (the harder "×" siblings become the new loud witnesses). Kept as sibling nominal readers rather than folding into one deriver-with-a-flag, matching how the additive family already reads two count sources with two anchored regexes.* (2026-07-23) |

(Don't apply Weakness and Resistance for Benched Pokémon.)"** — a SECONDARY snipe AFTER the main damage (which rides the attack's own `damage` field) — now SIMULATES. It is the SAME **`damageChosen`** op D57 built (count 1, `deals: true`) but WITHOUT `perTakenPrize` (a FIXED N, not Prize-scaled), so it is **ZERO new op or interpreter code** — just a new anchored derive **`ALSO_BENCHED_SNIPE`** (effects.ts) and one case in `deriveAttackEffect`, producing `[{op:"damageChosen", target:"opponentBench", amount:N, count:1, deals:true}]`. The main hit and the rider coexist by the normal attack flow: attack.ts deals the `damage`-field base to the Defender (through W/R) FIRST, then the effect program runs the benched snipe (parks on a count-1 choice, or auto-takes a Bench of one, or whiffs on an empty Bench). ### The `ALSO_BENCHED_SNIPE` guard (regex def)
`packages/engine/src/effects.ts:1115-1118`
```ts
const ALSO_BENCHED_SNIPE = new RegExp(
  `^This attack also does (\\d+) damage to 1 of your opponent['’]s Benched Pokémon\\.` +
    `(?: \\(Don['’]t apply Weakness and Resistance for Benched Pokémon\\.\\))?$`,
);
```

Its dispatch case — `packages/engine/src/effects.ts:1363-1369`:
```ts
match = ALSO_BENCHED_SNIPE.exec(effect);
if (match !== null) {
  const amount = Number(match[1]);

    return [{ op: "damageChosen", target: "opponentBench", amount, count: 1, deals: true }];

```

- `BENCHED_SNIPE_TAKEN_PRIZES` (Covetous Ivy, Prize-scaled) def `effects.ts:1099-1103`, dispatch `effects.ts:1340-1355`.


**The deriver-family tests (all in `packages/engine/src/`):**
- `alsoBenchedSnipe.test.ts` (192 lines) — the flat benched rider. **Contains the exact count-2 refusal you're relaxing:** `alsoBenchedSnipe.test.ts:90-91` (`// "2 of" — count ≠ 1.` then the text, asserted `toBeNull()` in the loop at line 97). // @luminous/engine — deterministic, pure PTCG game engine (P3).
//
// M1 surface: the setup sequence (shuffle, coin flip, hands + mulligans +
// compensation, placements, prizes), the turn loop with its mandatory draw
// and deck-out loss, energy attach, bench plays, retreat and pass. M2 adds
// the attack step: costs, weakness/resistance damage, Knock Outs with prize
// taking and forced promotion, and the full §14 win check — resolved through
// a staged turn tail that can park on player decisions. M3 adds the Special
// Conditions (§12) with their attack/retreat gates and the confusion flip,
// the Pokémon Checkup (§13) with its ticks, recoveries and KOs, and the
// first text-derived attack effects (effects.ts). M4 begins with evolution
// (§10): an Evolution card placed on an in-play Pokémon whose top card it
// evolves from, carrying over damage/energy/tools and clearing Special
// Conditions, under the §4/§10 timing rules. Spec:
// docs/workstreams/simulator.md; ruleset: docs/reference/ptcg-rules.md.
// Everything is (state, action) → result: no classes, no wall clock, no
// unseeded randomness — the same seed and actions replay identically. The
// package is shared by the web app (local play + the semantic animation
// event stream) and the api Worker (authoritative online matches, P4).

import type { ApplyResult, GameAction } from "./actions";
import { err } from "./actions";
import { attack, promote, takePrizes } from "./attack";
import { attachTool, playTrainer, rareCandy, resolveEffect, useAbility } from "./cardplay";
import { concede } from "./flow";
import {
  chooseFirstPlayer,
  setupDrawExtra,
  setupPlaceActive,
  setupPlaceBench,
  setupReady,
} from "./setup";
import { attachEnergy, endTurn, evolve, playBasicToBench, retreat } from "./turn";
import type { GameState, Seat } from "./types";

/** Engine milestone marker (M5 op-slice: **`attachFromTop`** — the from-the-top
    ATTACH the lookAtTopN slice deferred. Look at the top N of your own deck and
    attach the Energy you find there straight onto your Pokémon, "**in any way you
    like**" — so each attached card names its OWN destination, and the answer is a
    MAP (card → Pokémon) rather than the flat list every other card prompt takes
    (the new `attachCards` prompt). Two consumers differing in every rider the op
    has: **Electric Generator** (Item — top 5, up to 2 Basic {L} Energy CARDS, onto
    your BENCHED {L} Pokémon) and **Hydreigon "Tri Howl"** (Ability, once per turn
    — top 3, ANY number of Energy cards, onto ANY of your Pokémon).

    The leftovers clause is the design point: "Shuffle the other cards back" is a
    trailing `shuffleDeck` op (those cards never left the deck), but "**Discard**
    the other cards" must name exactly the looked-at cards that were not attached,
    so it is `discardRest` ON the op — and it fires on the whiff and the decline
    too, which is the difference between Tri Howl costing three cards and costing
    nothing. The filter reads the PRINT (`basicEnergy` / `anyEnergy`), never
    `providesEnergy`: these cards sit in a DECK, attached to nothing (§6.5).
    providesEnergy was 0.24.0; the discardEnergy attack arms 0.23.0;
    attackEpilogue/park 0.22.0; discardEnergy 0.21.0; board conditions 0.20.0).

    **0.26.0 — `payFromHand`, the printed COST that parks.** "You can use
    this card only if you discard 2 OTHER cards from your hand" (Ultra Ball,
    Earthen Vessel) and "You must discard a card from your hand in order to use
    this Ability" (Tinkaton, Revavroom, Meowscarada ex, Radiant Blastoise) are ONE
    mechanism in two printed wordings — and the "other" appears exactly when the
    paying card is itself in the hand, which is why the play GATE excludes the
    played uid and the op carries no flag. It is the FIRST op of its program, so
    the payment happens before what it buys: Revavroom pays, THEN draws to a hand
    size that counts the payment. MANDATORY and exact, so `chooseCards` gained a
    `min` (0 for every printed "up to", `count` here — the one park with no
    decline) and a `"discard"` destination; `AbilityProgram.cost` is GONE, its one
    consumer migrated onto the op it was the fungible special case of.

    **0.27.0 — the printed number is a FLOOR, and the cost that is not a
    discard.** Two mandatory-exactly-N fixes, one on each prompt that could
    already say "up to". (1) `choosePokemonMulti` gained `min`/`max` +
    `declinable`: "put 3 damage counters on **1** of your opponent's Benched
    Pokémon" is not "up to 1", so Meowscarada ex / Radiant Blastoise can no longer
    pay an irreversible hand cost and then place nothing, while Hawlucha's printed
    "**you may** choose 2" stays all-or-nothing — 2 or none, never 1 of 2 — which
    is a decline the framework's auto-fired triggers leave nowhere else to live.
    (2) `discardFromHandCost` became **`payFromHand`** with a required
    destination: `to: "deckBottom"` pays UNDER THE DECK, landing **Dendra** ×3
    ("Put a card from your hand on the bottom of your deck. If you do, draw cards
    until you have 5") — nothing is discarded, yet the mechanism is the same
    mandatory pick, the same conditional benefit and the same printed play gate,
    which Dendra states as its contrapositive. HAND_COST_PAID carries `to`,
    because a payment to the discard becomes public and one to the deck never
    does. **Skwovet** ×2 ("Nest Stash") reaches the same destination with the
    WHOLE hand and needed no new op at all — `handRefresh` with Iono's `toBottom`
    + `onlyIfAnyMoved`.

    **0.28.0 — a clause can read what an earlier clause DID (§9.2).** The
    engine's first op→op data flow: an op files the uids it moved under a named
    `EffectSlot`, and a later op in the same program reads them. Two readers, one
    record — the printed "in this way" / "if you do" is a new `recordGate` (the
    third and last gate, spliced like the other two), and "you can't choose a card
    you discarded with the effect of this card" is `discardPileRetrieval.exclude`.

    would have been wrong on the very first card that needed this.

    onto your Pokémon, the deck-search sibling of `attachFromTop`. It shares that
    op's `attachCards` MAP prompt (the printed clause is the same one) and differs

    effect is running — the printed "this Pokémon" — set at every run site that
    knows it (an activated Ability's own Pokémon, a trigger's, the attacker) and
    ABSENT for a Trainer program, which has no such Pokémon. Constant for the
    run, rides the continuation across parks (JSON, D14). First reader:
    `attachFromDeck.toSelf`, the third printed target rule ("attach it to THIS
    Pokémon"), which lands **Pawmot** ×2 ("Electrogenesis") — a benched Pawmot
    feeds ITSELF, the exact sentence no seat-relative target rule could say.

    0.31.0 — `healChosen.upTo`: the printed "up to N … each" heal (Saguaro ×3,
    "Choose up to 2 of your Pokémon and heal 50 damage from each of them") —
    the first consumer of choosePokemonMulti's min: 0 end (§9.1's "up to"
    legalizes 0..max), parked at every non-empty board with §8.6 clamping the
    ask.

    0.32.0 — `bottomFromOpponentHand` + `opponentMayDraw`: the opponent reveals
    their hand (a new public HAND_REVEALED — every uid, because that is what
    the printed word means), the controller bottoms a chosen card onto the
    OPPONENT's deck (CARD_TO_BOTTOM_OF_DECK, named — the whole move happened
    face up), and the gated draw is the engine's first decision ANSWERED BY THE
    NON-CONTROLLER: the park carries a decider, the phase an `answerer` (absent
    when it is the controller, so every older park is byte-identical), and
    resolveEffect admits only that seat. Ortega ×2 authored (the Miriam shape
    across the table), Greavard "Underworld Stroll" DERIVED (the Supporter-
    filtered attack twin — its second attack is why the card-level registry
    `attack` field could not carry it). programPlayable gains the public-count
    empty-opponent-hand gate (the Catcher/Hammer class) and is now EXPORTED —
    the HUD greys with the predicate that rejects.

    0.33.0 — `damageSelf` + the TWO-seat attack epilogue: the recoil clause "This
    Pokémon also does N damage to itself" (Skeledirge sv01-038 "Blazing Shout")
    is the engine's first attack that damages its OWN board, placed flat as
    COUNTERS_PLACED source "self" (the confusion self-hit's model, OUTSIDE the
    §8.5 W/R pipeline). finishAttack's KO sweep widened from the single defender
    seat to BOTH, in [defender, attacker] order so §8.1's "the player whose turn
    it is takes their Prizes first" holds, and a self-KO prizes to the defender.
    This makes the §14 double-KO tie reachable from the attack path for the first
    time — collectKnockOuts' existing speculative guard owns it (the D42 debt,
    paid).

    0.34.0 — count-scaled attack damage (the additive "+" family): the printed
    "This attack does N more damage for each damage counter on this Pokémon"
    (Paldean Tauros sv02-028 "Raging Horns", fix-attacker "Rage") is now SIMULATED
    — `deriveAttackDamageBonus` folds N × (the attacker's OWN damage counters) into
    the base BEFORE the §8.5 W/R pipeline (attack.ts), alongside the continuous
    Vitality Band bonus. The new DAMAGE_DEALT `scaled` field carries it (present
    only when it applied), and the "+"/text is no longer flagged loudly for these
    cards. Charizard ex sv03-125 "Burning Darkness" (a DIFFERENT count source — the
    opponent's taken Prizes) STAYS on the ATTACK_EFFECT_SKIPPED path, the
    anchor-guard witness proving the deriver is narrow.

    0.35.0 — the count union's SECOND member: Charizard ex sv03-125 "Burning
    Darkness" (180+, "… for each Prize card your opponent has taken") now SIMULATES,
    folding 30 × (the opponent's TAKEN Prizes = 6 − their remaining pile) into the
    base. `scaledAttackDamage` widened to reach the opponent's board; the
    unsimulated-"+" witness moved to Entei sv03-030 (an attached-Energy count
    source, still no reader). The "×"/multiply Prize family (Pecharunt ex — no
    "more") stays loud.

    0.36.0 — the "×"/multiply damage family, the additive family's sibling: "This
    attack does N damage for each Prize card your opponent has taken." (NO "more" —
    Pecharunt ex sv06.5-039 60×, Annihilape sv01-109 70×) now SIMULATES. It reuses
    the additive family's `opponentPrizesTaken` count evaluator UNCHANGED via a new
    reader `deriveAttackDamageMultiplier`; the only difference is the fold — the
    printed "N×" base is the per-unit, so it is DROPPED and `per × count` is the
    WHOLE damage (count 0 → 0 damage), where the additive family adds `per × count`
    onto a printed base. Wo-Chien ex (benched-target) and Chien-Pao ex
    (discarded-Energy count) stay loud, the anchor-guard witnesses.

    0.37.0 — the "×"/multiply family's benched-TARGET sibling: Wo-Chien ex sv02-027
    "Covetous Ivy" ("This attack does 60 damage to 1 of your opponent's Benched
    Pokémon for each Prize card your opponent has taken.") now SIMULATES. Its target
    is one CHOSEN Benched Pokémon rather than the Defender, so it is NOT the pre-W/R
    Defender fold (D56) but a `damageChosen` op — the put-counter snipe (Hawlucha /
    Meowscarada) extended with `deals` (ATTACK DAMAGE, a DAMAGE_DEALT with the
    benched reduction passive, not a flat placed counter) and `perTakenPrize` (the
    amount is `60 × the opponent's taken Prizes`, read from state in the interpreter;
    0 taken → no damage and no pick). The "6 − remaining" Prize formula is now the
    shared `takenPrizes` helper (types.ts), used by both this and the D55/D56 fold.
    Chien-Pao ex "Hail Blade" (a DISCARDED-Energy count, and a PRE-damage park) stays
    loud, the remaining "×" sibling.

    0.38.0 — the flat benched-snipe RIDER family: "This attack ALSO does N damage to 1
    of your opponent's Benched Pokémon. (Don't apply Weakness and Resistance for
    Benched Pokémon.)" now SIMULATES — a SECONDARY snipe after the main damage (which
    rides the attack's own `damage` field). It is the SAME count-1 `deals` snipe as
    D57's Covetous Ivy WITHOUT `perTakenPrize` (a fixed N, not Prize-scaled), so it is
    a new derive `ALSO_BENCHED_SNIPE` and ZERO new op/interpreter code. Lands ~15
    prints across Miraidon / Tadbulb / Pawmot / Bellibolt / Decidueye ex / Jumpluff /
    Orthworm / Palafin / Pyroar / Dartrix. Flamigo's "If Flamigo is on your Bench, …"
    (a board-condition gate) and the "each of" / "2 of" / "1 of YOUR Benched" variants
    stay loud, each a different shape.

    0.39.0 — the ANY-target snipe family: "This attack does N damage to 1 of your
    opponent's Pokémon." (the WHOLE attack — the Active OR a Bench) now SIMULATES.
    `damageChosen` gained a `target: "opponentAny"` mode (candidates = the opponent's
    Active + Bench, via `oppAnyRefs`), and `placeSnipe` an Active arm (`snipeActive`):
    a snipe that lands on the ACTIVE runs the §8.5 W/R pipeline (base → ×Weakness →
    −Resistance → −reduction), where a Benched target stays flat — the rules'
    "Weakness/Resistance apply only to the Active" made conditional on the pick.
    Fezandipiti ex sv06.5-038 "Cruel Arrow" (100), Rotom sv01-069 "Linear Attack"
    (20), Paldean Tauros "Aqua Dive", Bellibolt ex, Kilowattrel. Umbreon "Feint
    Attack" (a different W/R-immunity wording), Pawmot ex (a discard cost), and
    Magikarp (a coin flip) stay loud.

    0.40.0 — the authoritative per-viewer REDACTOR (P4 online, increment 1c). The
    engine gains `redactGame(state, seat) → RedactedGame` (redact.ts): the PURE
    server-side hidden-information filter the lobby Durable Object runs once per
    connected socket, so no full `GameState` (opponent hand/deck/prizes) ever
    crosses the network. It restates the web app's playmat redaction (opponent
    hand/prizes/decks as counts, setup in-play as anonymous backs) against the
    neutral `@luminous/schema` `RedactedGame` wire shape — no image URLs, no
    engine imports on the far side. Its subtle phase derivation (turn owner /
    who-must-act / parked interrupt / outcome) is the exhaustive `phaseViewOf`
    switch, MOVED here from that projection (phaseView.ts) so both share one
    source; the web projection now imports it. No game-logic change — this slice
    adds a read surface, not a rule.

    0.41.0 — CONCEDE (P4 online, increment 3c-ii). The first change to the win
    vocabulary since M1: `GameOverReason` gains **`conceded`** and a new
    `concede(state, action)` (flow.ts, beside `finishGame`) hands the game to the
    opponent. Unlike every other action it is legal in ANY phase but `gameOver` —
    a concede that only worked on your own turn would be useless in the situations
    it exists for (an opponent who walked away mid-turn, a park nobody can answer),
    and it is the one action that can always END a match that is otherwise stuck.
    ONE reason covers both triggers — a player pressing concede, and the P4 server
    forfeiting for a player who abandoned an online match — because to the opponent
    they are the same event, and the engine has no business knowing about sockets.
    This IS a rules-surface change (a new way a game can end), hence the minor
    bump; the two reason→prose maps (log.ts `GAME_OVER_REASONS`, the web's
    `GAME_OVER_DETAIL`) became total Records in the same pass, so a future reason
    is a compile error rather than silently rendering as "the deck ran out".

    0.42.0 — DEFIANCE BAND (P3-M5, the `conditionalDamageBonus` row). The D40
    `BoardCondition` vocabulary's third consumer, and its first PASSIVE one — the
    conditional twin of Vitality Band. `PassiveEffects` gains
    `damageBonusBeforeWRIf: { amount, cond }` (Tool: "+30 before W/R while you
    have more Prize cards remaining than your opponent"). continuous.ts stays the
    single seat-FREE aggregation point, now collecting these gated bonuses RAW in
    a `conditionalDamageBonusBeforeWR` list; the fold lives in interpreter.ts's
    new `attackerPreWRBonus`, shared by the two pre-W/R read sites (attack.ts's
    main hit + `snipeActive`), so the condition is evaluated ONCE beside the sole
    `conditionHolds` — the only place that knows the attacker's seat, which a
    BoardCondition is relative to. Kept out of the unconditional
    `damageBonusBeforeWR` so the defender-reduction / HP reads cannot be credited
    an attacker's conditional bonus. Reuses `morePrizesThanOpponent` (no new
    condition), so it is a card row + one new passive field, not a new primitive.
    No web change (damage bonuses are engine-internal, surfaced only via the
    `DAMAGE_DEALT` log event). Choice Belt — the row's other card — is a
    target-type gate ("…Active Pokémon V"), a different shape, left for its slice.

    0.43.0 — CHOICE BELT (P3-M5, the `conditionalDamageBonus` row's 2nd and last
    card). The target-gated twin of Vitality Band: +30 before W/R, but only when
    the DEFENDER is a Pokémon V. `PassiveEffects` gains a sibling field
    `damageBonusBeforeWRIfTarget: { amount, targetSuffix }`, aggregated seat-free
    by continuous.ts into a new `targetConditionalDamageBonusBeforeWR` list and
    folded at the two pre-W/R read sites via the SAME `attackerPreWRBonus`, which
    now also takes the `defenderCard` (both the main hit and `snipeActive` had it
    in hand). The "is a Pokémon V" test needs no schema/ingest/DB change: the
    suffix tcgdex drops at ingest is ALSO printed in the card NAME, which IS
    persisted, so a new `cards.ts pokemonSuffixOf` derives it from `name`,
    reading "V" LITERALLY (a VMAX/VSTAR defender is untouched). The current
    SV-era pool holds no Pokémon V, so the gate is dormant against the live
    catalog and correct — it fires once a prior-era set is ingested. Distinct
    from Defiance Band's field because the gate reads the DEFENDER, not the
    attacker's board, so it is NOT the D40 `BoardCondition` vocabulary. No
    web/API/DB/schema change (damage bonuses stay engine-internal).

    0.44.0 — PRIZE VALUE (P3-M5, §8.1). `prizeValueOf` stops returning 1 for every
    KO: a VMAX is worth 3 Prizes, any other rule box (ex / V / VSTAR / GX) 2, a
    plain body 1. The class is read off `pokemonSuffixOf` (the rule-box marker the
    NAME still carries after ingest drops tcgdex's `suffix`), so — like Choice Belt
    (0.43.0) — no schema/ingest/DB change was needed to value an ex at its two
    Prizes. The `count` this feeds was already a variable at the two prize read
    sites (flow.ts's takePrizes stage + the §14 tie-guard speculation), both of
    which clamp to the Prizes that remain, so a 2-Prize KO with one Prize left
    takes the last one and wins rather than over-drawing — no flow change. The
    feared blast radius never landed: every existing KO test knocks out a plain
    body, so the whole suite stayed green; the new behaviour is pinned by a new
    prizeValue.test.ts (the KO→count wiring, on a dedicated mulligan-free
    PRIZE_DECK) plus unit cases in cards.test.ts. No longer dormant against the
    live SV-era pool, which is full of ex Pokémon. No web/API/DB/schema change. */

/** The one reducer. Dispatches on action type; each handler validates the
    phase and acting seat itself and returns ok/err without ever throwing
    or mutating its input.

    The two guards below are unreachable through the typed API but NOT through
    the wire: P4's authoritative Worker decodes actions from a client, and the
    never-throw contract has to hold for a bogus `type` or `seat` too (an
    unknown seat would otherwise index `players` with undefined and throw). */
export function applyAction(state: GameState, action: GameAction): ApplyResult {
  // A finished game accepts nothing further.
  if (state.phase.kind === "gameOver") {
    const outcome = state.phase.outcome;
    return err(
      "GAME_OVER",
      outcome.result === "win"
        ? `the game is over (${outcome.winner} won: ${outcome.reason})`
        : "the game is over (tie)",
    );
  }
  if (!isSeat(action.seat)) {
    return err("UNKNOWN_SEAT", `"${String(action.seat)}" is not a seat`);
  }
  switch (action.type) {
    case "chooseFirstPlayer":
      return chooseFirstPlayer(state, action);
    case "setupDrawExtra":
      return setupDrawExtra(state, action);
    case "setupPlaceActive":
      return setupPlaceActive(state, action);
    case "setupPlaceBench":
      return setupPlaceBench(state, action);
    case "setupReady":
      return setupReady(state, action);
    case "attachEnergy":
      return attachEnergy(state, action);
    case "playBasicToBench":
      return playBasicToBench(state, action);
    case "evolve":
      return evolve(state, action);
    case "rareCandy":
      return rareCandy(state, action);
    case "retreat":
      return retreat(state, action);
    case "attack":
      return attack(state, action);
    case "playTrainer":
      return playTrainer(state, action);
    case "attachTool":
      return attachTool(state, action);
    case "useAbility":
      return useAbility(state, action);
    case "resolveEffect":
      return resolveEffect(state, action);
    case "takePrizes":
      return takePrizes(state, action);
    case "promote":
      return promote(state, action);
    case "endTurn":
      return endTurn(state, action);
    case "concede":
      return concede(state, action);
    default:
      return err("UNKNOWN_ACTION", `unknown action type "${(action as { type: string }).type}"`);
  }
}

function isSeat(value: unknown): value is Seat {
  return value === "p1" || value === "p2";
}

| D94 | Spread "also" rider — one optional token, and a deviation from the resume point's ordering toward the candidate with real yield (P3-M5, engine 0.45.0) | The each-of-spread also-rider: "This attack **also** does N damage to each of your opponent's Benched Pokémon." (Cetoddle sv02-053 "Avalanche" — 30 to the Active, then 10 to each Bench). **A one-token regex relaxation, ZERO new op/interpreter/registry code:** the word "also" is made OPTIONAL in the existing `SPREAD_EACH_BENCH` deriver (`^This attack (?:also )?does …`), so the rider derives to the **same** `spreadDamage` op as the bare "This attack does N …" form. **Design call — one rule, not a twin.** The snipe family has separate anchored regexes per shape because "1 of" vs "each of" pick genuinely different ops (`damageChosen` vs `spreadDamage`); here the string AFTER "does" is identical, and the engine already treats even the bare spread as a SECONDARY hit (the main damage rides the attack's own `damage` field — comment predates this slice), so "also" is pure emphasis of a fact the `damage` field already carries. A separate `ALSO_SPREAD_EACH_BENCH` regex + dispatch case would be a redundant twin producing a byte-identical op, so it was rejected in favour of the optional token. **A test moved, not just added:** `alsoBenchedSnipe.test.ts` listed this exact "each of" text as a `toBeNull()` near-miss — but it was null only because NO reader accepted it; now `SPREAD_EACH_BENCH` correctly claims it, so the assertion flipped from "refused" to "derives to `spreadDamage`", preserving the test's real intent (the single-target `damageChosen` snipe reader must never grab a spread). Pinned by a derive assertion on the verbatim Cetoddle text in `knockout.test.ts`; the full §8.5 spread flow (bench W/R, Bouffer reduction, bench KO) is already covered by `fix-sniper`'s Spread Shot, so re-driving an identical op through a Cetoddle deck would be redundant. **The DEVIATION worth recording:** the resume point ranked "count-2" (a benched/any-target snipe to "2 of your opponent's Pokémon") FIRST as cheapest. But there is no committed card corpus (attack text is fetched from tcgdex at runtime), and the backlog names **no concrete SV card for count-2** while it names Cetoddle for the spread rider. A live tcgdex query CONFIRMED Cetoddle sv02-053 prints this text verbatim; count-2 remains a "family-completeness, dormant, no known consumer" relaxation. Per conventions ("prefer the first unless the code tells you otherwise"), the corpus reality — one candidate authors a real live card, the other zero verifiable cards — is exactly that signal, so this session took the spread rider. count-2 stays on the backlog, honestly labelled as dormant/unverified. **No web/API/DB/schema change** (a deriver-only slice; `spreadDamage` is engine-internal, surfaced via `DAMAGE_DEALT`). engineVersion 0.44.0 → **0.45.0**; 1958 → **1960** tests (138 files). `bun run check` green. **Self-reviewed, no independent reviewer** — a one-token relaxation of a just-verified regex. *Why: the two open candidates were equal in cost but not in value — verifying the actual catalog (rather than trusting the "cheapest first" label) showed one fires against a real card and the other against none, so "better and green" meant taking the one with yield.* (2026-07-27) |

Defaulting the missing fields on read — the fix the LOW originally proposed — was REJECTED: it repairs only the fields we happen to know went missing, and says nothing about the far more dangerous case, an embedded engine `GameState` written by a build whose RULES have since moved, which reads back "fine" and then plays subtly wrong. A version covers both, and it is what makes "no migrations" a loud, recoverable condition instead of a silent hazard. | D80 | Half-open sockets are swept with the runtime's OWN keepalive timestamp (P4 online, increment 3c-viii) | The gap 3c-v's browser run surfaced, and the last known way an online match could stall. `setWebSocketAutoResponse` answers the client's 1.5s ping without waking the DO — the thing that makes hibernation worth having — but it also means the DO can never notice pings that STOP. ## Locked assumptions (override explicitly if they change)
- Bun-workspace monorepo; API + Lobby DO on Cloudflare **Workers** via `wrangler`.
- **Hono** + **Zod**; **Drizzle** over D1. Ingest uses **plain REST fetch +
  our Zod schemas** — the official `@tcgdex/sdk` turned out unnecessary since
  we validate every payload ourselves anyway (changed 2026-07-09, was: SDK).
- Server **sessions** (http-only cookie), not stateless JWT.
- Ingest filters to SV-era but writes the full-history schema.
- attacks/weaknesses/resistances stored as JSON columns for now (promote to
  child tables only if we need to query inside them).
- English (`en`) first; schema leaves room for i18n later.
- The **match engine (P3)** is the actual gameplay; approximate at first,
  improved iteratively.

## These are defaults, not law
Every decision and assumption here is a **default with a rationale**, chosen with
the context available at the time — revisit any of them when the code or new
context reveals a better path. The point of writing them down is to preserve the
*why*, so a later session can judge whether it still holds.

## Adding / changing a decision
Append a row (or a dated subsection for bigger ones) with the choice **and the
one-line why**. When you revise an existing decision, update its row and note
what changed and why. The one hard rule: **don't reverse a decision silently** —
leave a trail so the reasoning is never lost.

### Prior header (P4 3c-viii — half-open socket liveness, kept for continuity)
**Last updated (was):** 2026-07-26 — build session #63 (**P4 3c-viii — half-open socket liveness**). The gap
3c-v's browser run surfaced, and the last known way an online match could stall. `setWebSocketAutoResponse`
answers the client's 1.5s ping WITHOUT waking the DO — the thing that makes hibernation worth having — but it
also means the DO can never notice pings that **stop**. A network that dies without a TCP close therefore
left a socket that looked perfectly live forever: `hasSocket` said yes, no disconnect grace was armed, no
forfeit clock started, and the opponent waited indefinitely. Every ORDINARY exit (tab close, browser kill,
navigation, reload, crash) delivers a close event, which is why this never bit in practice and why it took a
deliberate `set offline` to reproduce. **The fix reads the signal the runtime was already recording:**
`state.getWebSocketAutoResponseTimestamp(ws)` returns when it last auto-answered that socket, so liveness
costs nothing at ping time. The alternative — dropping the auto-response and stamping `lastSeen` in
`webSocketMessage` — was rejected on exactly that ground: ~40 wakes a minute per socket, hibernation given
up, to learn what the runtime already knows. **What it costs instead is a POLL,** because a quiet in-game
lobby schedules no alarm at all: `scheduleMaintenance` now pushes a **`LIVENESS_SWEEP_MS`** (30s) deadline
whenever any socket is connected, so an occupied lobby wakes twice a minute. **`SOCKET_SILENCE_MS`** is 15s —
ten missed pings, so a phone changing networks or a throttled background tab is not mistaken for a dead one —
and a test pins the budget that matters: sweep + silence + the 5s grace all fit inside the 90s forfeit, so a
dead network can never resolve SLOWER than a closed tab. A `null` timestamp counts as **ALIVE**, deliberately:
it is the state of every connection before its first ping, and nothing can distinguish "just opened" from
"opened long ago and never pinged". **The sweep only CLOSES** — the grace, the seat going disconnected and
the forfeit are all machinery a real close already drives, reached through the same `socketGone` (called
explicitly, since a server-side `close()` delivers no `webSocketClose` event to us). engine RULES UNCHANGED
(0.41.0); 1874 → **1878** tests. `bun run check` green. Built solo with full context; **self-reviewed, no
independent reviewer this session**. **BROWSER-VERIFIED with the very reproducer that exposed the bug:** with
a match live, one client was put offline with its socket left OPEN — before this change that produced nothing
at all, and now the opponent saw "disconnected — forfeits in 1:30" after ~50s (15s silence + up to 30s sweep
+ the 5s grace) with the countdown running. Bringing the client back online restored it within ~10s (the
channel reconnected, re-helloed, the forfeit was cancelled), while the client that stayed connected
throughout was never swept. Zero page errors. **With this, P4 has no known defects and no planned work left.**

countdown ends up promising something the server won't do. **The invariant that makes it safe is `connected`

argument defaulting to null (so you cannot write one without deciding the other), and

normalizer that fills fields added since the write — deliberately the OPPOSITE of D72's `MatchRecord` answer,

### Prior resume point (P3-M5 board conditions, kept for continuity)
**Board conditions are live (P3-M5, D40) — one `BoardCondition` vocabulary, TWO
consumers.** The `conditionalPlay` family, built as a primitive instead of a per-card
flag. **`BoardCondition`** (effects.ts) is a predicate union evaluated for ONE seat —
**`morePrizesThanOpponent`** (strict `>`: you are BEHIND on Prizes taken),
**`yourStadiumInPlay`**, **`noEnergyOnYourPokemon`** (Active AND Bench, Basic or
Special) — behind a single evaluator **`conditionHolds`** and a printed-text describer
**`conditionNote`**. **The invariant IS the design: every member reads only PUBLIC
state**, which is exactly why **a gate emits no event** — contrast `coinFlipGate`,
whose flip is genuinely new information; a board condition is a fact both players can
read off the table, and the branch's own ops emit whatever happened.
**Consumer A — the printed PLAY GATE:** `CardProgram.trainerPlayableIf`, checked by
`playTrainer` BEFORE the card leaves hand (new `ErrorCode` `PLAY_CONDITION_NOT_MET`),
so a failed gate costs nothing. Categorically different from `programPlayable`'s
would-only-whiff heuristics: this is a rule PRINTED on the card. Named `trainer…`
because it is honoured on EXACTLY one path — `playStadium`/`rareCandy`/`attachTool`/
`useAbility` all return before it and would ignore it SILENTLY (the `trainerEndsTurn`
precedent; it is also why Luxray's Ability gate must NOT be authored here).
**Consumer B — the mid-program branch:** the **`conditionGate`** op
`{cond, then, otherwise?}`, spliced into runProgram's work queue exactly like
`coinFlipGate` (an op inside a branch can still park, and a branch may hold further
gates), evaluated against the board AS OF the gate. One-armed is the common shape
(Falkner); `otherwise` is the printed "…**instead**", a real if/ELSE (Grusha).
**One tiny new automatic op — `drawUntilHandSize`:** it DRAWS to a floor and never
TRIMS a bigger hand, and at a count ≤ 0 it no-ops with NO event (no misleading "drew 0

alone** and append it UNDER the deck (`[...deck, ...shuffle(hand)]`) instead of
shuffling it into the deck, so the deck's existing order — and therefore the very next
draws — SURVIVE (the whole strategic point of Iono over Judge; pinned by a test
asserting the drawn cards are EXACTLY the pre-play deck top, in order).

count (the player behind draws more); a Prize count is public, so the draw size leaks
nothing. **`onlyIfAnyMoved?: true`** — the draw clause fires only if ≥1 affected player
actually moved ≥1 card: an **all-or-nothing gate ACROSS the seats** ("if EITHER
player…"), not per-seat. That gate forced the op's one structural change: **two passes**
over the affected seats (all placements, then all draws) instead of D38's interleaved
move-then-draw — **behaviour-preserving** for Youngster/Judge/Brassius/Katy (per-seat

### Prior header (P4 3c-viii — half-open socket liveness, kept for continuity)
**Last updated (was):** 2026-07-26 — build session #63 (**P4 3c-viii — half-open socket liveness**). The gap
3c-v's browser run surfaced, and the last known way an online match could stall. `setWebSocketAutoResponse`
answers the client's 1.5s ping WITHOUT waking the DO — the thing that makes hibernation worth having — but it
also means the DO can never notice pings that **stop**. A network that dies without a TCP close therefore
left a socket that looked perfectly live forever: `hasSocket` said yes, no disconnect grace was armed, no
forfeit clock started, and the opponent waited indefinitely. Every ORDINARY exit (tab close, browser kill,
navigation, reload, crash) delivers a close event, which is why this never bit in practice and why it took a
deliberate `set offline` to reproduce. **The fix reads the signal the runtime was already recording:**
`state.getWebSocketAutoResponseTimestamp(ws)` returns when it last auto-answered that socket, so liveness
costs nothing at ping time. The alternative — dropping the auto-response and stamping `lastSeen` in
`webSocketMessage` — was rejected on exactly that ground: ~40 wakes a minute per socket, hibernation given
up, to learn what the runtime already knows. **What it costs instead is a POLL,** because a quiet in-game
lobby schedules no alarm at all: `scheduleMaintenance` now pushes a **`LIVENESS_SWEEP_MS`** (30s) deadline
whenever any socket is connected, so an occupied lobby wakes twice a minute. **`SOCKET_SILENCE_MS`** is 15s —
ten missed pings, so a phone changing networks or a throttled background tab is not mistaken for a dead one —
and a test pins the budget that matters: sweep + silence + the 5s grace all fit inside the 90s forfeit, so a
dead network can never resolve SLOWER than a closed tab. A `null` timestamp counts as **ALIVE**, deliberately:
it is the state of every connection before its first ping, and nothing can distinguish "just opened" from
"opened long ago and never pinged". **The sweep only CLOSES** — the grace, the seat going disconnected and
the forfeit are all machinery a real close already drives, reached through the same `socketGone` (called
explicitly, since a server-side `close()` delivers no `webSocketClose` event to us). engine RULES UNCHANGED
(0.41.0); 1874 → **1878** tests. `bun run check` green. Built solo with full context; **self-reviewed, no
independent reviewer this session**. **BROWSER-VERIFIED with the very reproducer that exposed the bug:** with
a match live, one client was put offline with its socket left OPEN — before this change that produced nothing
at all, and now the opponent saw "disconnected — forfeits in 1:30" after ~50s (15s silence + up to 30s sweep
+ the 5s grace) with the countdown running. Bringing the client back online restored it within ~10s (the
channel reconnected, re-helloed, the forfeit was cancelled), while the client that stayed connected
throughout was never swept. Zero page errors. **With this, P4 has no known defects and no planned work left.**
